Article Title: 'They are from his film fan base': Congress MLA brushes aside TVK’s 'Vijay for PM' pitch
Article Text:
Tamil Nadu CM C Joseph Vijay

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu Congress MLA Tharahai Cuthbert on Wednesday dismissed ally TVK’s projection of its leader, C Joseph Vijay, as the prime ministerial candidate for the 2029 Lok Sabha elections, saying TVK leaders were making the claim as “fans” of the chief minister, a reference to Vijay’s past as an actor.“They are TVK MLAs, they are all still in the fan basis. They have come from a fan--film industries as a fan basis. Definitely, they will be saying that,” Cuthbert told reporters in Chennai.She added that, politically, the leaders had taken a “stern decision” that Congress leader Rahul Gandhi would be the candidate for the prime minister’s post in 2029.Cuthbert’s remarks come amid growing differences over the political positioning of the two parties, with TVK leaders repeatedly projecting Vijay as a possible national leader.TVK leader and Tamil Nadu minister Aadhav Arjuna had earlier asserted that the country’s top constitutional office should be held by a leader from Tamil Nadu.Responding to the remarks by TVK leaders, Congress leader and state Tourism Minister S Rajesh Kumar warned that the two Congress ministers in the TVK-led Tamil Nadu government would resign if the Vijay-led party did not accept Rahul Gandhi as the prime ministerial candidate.The Congress ended its long-standing alliance with the DMK following the Tamil Nadu assembly elections in April and extended support to TVK, which emerged as the single-largest party but fell short of the majority mark. The Congress backed TVK along with the VCK, IUML, CPI and CPI(M), with the stated condition that “communal forces” be kept out of the government.Vijay launched TVK in February 2024, becoming the latest Tamil film star to enter state politics.The Congress last led a government at the Centre from 2004 to 2014.
Article Summary: Tamil nadu congress mla tharahai cuthbert dismissed ally tvk’s projection of its leader, c joseph vijay, as the prime ministerial candidate for the 2029 lok sabha elections. She said tvk leaders were making the claim as “fans” of the chief minister, a reference to vijay's past as an actor.

Article Title: Northeast faces new vector threat as diseases spread to new areas: Health panel
Article Text:
Sikkim recorded the highest incidence among Northeast states, with 374 dengue cases in 2024. Using the state’s revised population estimate, the dengue incidence was 57.9 per lakh.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Climate change, deforestation, unplanned urbanisation and poor drainage are creating conditions for mosquitoes and other disease-carrying vectors to spread into new areas of the Northeast, a parliamentary health panel has warned, calling for targeted, technology-driven surveillance and prevention strategies.The Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health and Family Welfare, in its report on vector-borne diseases in North-East India, said the region's difficult terrain, changing rainfall and temperature patterns, rapid urbanisation and gaps in healthcare access were contributing to the persistence and geographical expansion of these diseases.The numbers show a sharp rise in dengue in the region. Reported cases increased from 142 in 2014 to 19,761 in 2023, before falling to 7,186 in 2024. The report records 1,524 cases in 2025 through August, making it a partial-year figure and therefore not directly comparable with full-year totals.Chikungunya cases in the region increased from 3,493 in 2023 to 3,991 in 2024, an increase of about 14.3%.The panel said dengue and chikungunya are increasingly urban concerns, driven by urbanisation, water-storage practices, poor waste management, climate change and population movement.Sikkim recorded the highest incidence among Northeast states, with 374 dengue cases in 2024. Using the state’s revised population estimate, the dengue incidence was 57.9 per lakh. Sikkim also reported 1,863 chikungunya cases, with an incidence of 291.2 per lakh in 2024.Malaria, however, presents a more mixed picture. Across India, the number of high-burden districts with an Annual Parasite Index above one fell from 155 in 2015 to 37 in 2024. In the Northeast, 16 districts in Arunachal Pradesh and six in Nagaland have reported zero indigenous malaria cases for the past three years.Japanese encephalitis remains another concern, particularly in Assam and other northeastern states. The report records 885 JE cases in the Northeast in 2024, compared with 709 in 2023. Nationally, the JE fatality rate fell substantially, from 17.6% in 2014 to 7.1% in 2024.The panel recommended real-time surveillance through a dedicated Northeast vector-borne disease portal and AI-based early-warning systems to predict hotspots, along with mobile health units, pre-monsoon camps, rapid-response teams, stronger labs and dedicated NESIDS funding for high-risk areas. It also called for disease-specific treatment protocols for severe dengue and other complications, a Regional Entomology Training Hub, and greater use of climate modelling and digital reporting. The panel flagged a data gap too: vector-borne disease data are not separately collected for tribal, rural and urban populations, and recommended doing so for more targeted interventions.
Article Summary: Climate change, deforestation, unplanned urbanisation and poor drainage are creating conditions for mosquitoes and other disease-carrying vectors to spread into new areas of the northeast.

Article Title: Ram temple cash theft: Journalist accuses cops of digital tracking
Article Text:
Abhishek Upadhyay on Tuesday sought Supreme Court's intervention

Abhishek Upadhyay, the journalist who reported embezzlement of donations at Ayodhya's Ram temple, on Tuesday sought Supreme Court's intervention saying that Ghaziabad police have, in connection with a case of road rage against him, sought his digital footprints from social media platform X since June 1, which could jeopardise identities of sources who tipped him about the donation scam.His counsel Anoop P Awasthi told a bench led by CJI Surya Kant that Ghaziabad police's request to X HQ in California for the alleged road rage case of Aug 18 would result in gross violation of his right to privacy, adding that such data in the hands of police would reveal the identities of the sources who informed him about temple theft.The FIR concerns an alleged incident of Aug 18, yet the investigating agency seeks the petitioner's IP and account-related information from June 1, well before the alleged incident. No nexus between such sweeping historical digital information and the investigation of the alleged incident has been disclosed in the impugned notice," Upadhyay said in his application.The bench said it had on Aug 25 protected the journalist from coercive action by police in the road rage case and that his fresh application would be listed for hearing in due course.
Article Summary: Abhishek upadhyay reported embezzlement of donations at ayodhya's ram temple. Ghaziabad police have, in connection with a case of road rage against him, sought his digital footprints from social media platform x since june 1.

Article Title: Safai Karmachari Andolan counters govt reply in Parliament, claims manual scavenging still exists in atleast 46 districts
Article Text:
Muzaffar Ahmed Sheikh (35) from Ganderbal district in Jammu & Kashmir.

Mussi Devi (71) from Sitapur district in Uttar Pradesh

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Challenging the Centre’s claim made in Parliament in the monsoon session that a survey conducted in all districts of the country during the year 2024-25 found no person engaged as a manual scavenger, Safai Karmachari Andolan (SKA) on Tuesday brought together women from Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar and youth from Jammu & Kashmir claiming to be engaged in manual cleaning of human excreta in insanitary latrines to highlight that the illegal practice still persists in atleast 46 districts of these four states.National Convenor and co-founder of SKA, Bezwada Wilson said that they have evidence by way of photographs showing women lifting waste from dry latrines in these districts. “We will be writing to the ministry of social justice and empowerment to seek a fresh survey citing this evidence and demand action to stop the illegal practice in these districts within 60 days,” Wilson said.He, however, made it clear that if the ministry fails to act over the next two months, SKA teams will carry out a survey and put together a report by early next year. “We will highlight the findings across states and share them with Parliamentarians and the Judiciary to seek enforcement,” Wilson said.Former Supreme Court Judges Justice Madan Lokur and Justice Sudhandhu Dhulia and former Patna High Court Judge Justice Anjana Prakash expressed solidarity with the women and men who came forward to share heartwrenching experiences of a life marked by exploitation and untouchability despite the law in place wherein manual scavenging is illegal and dry latrines are banned.At the meeting held at Press Club of India as SKA announced the launch of a year long campaign ‘INDIA @ 80’ to free the country from manual scavenging, the former judges announced full support. Elaborating on the struggle by those involved in manual scavenging to break free, Justice Lokur expressed concern over the practice persisting despite the protection guaranteed by the Constitution of India against untouchability which is abolished and forbidden.He also dwelled on the long and continuing struggle for justice by those affected and how they have repeatedly ended up approaching the judiciary that has resulted in various directions from the Supreme Court from time to time. Justice Lokur highlighted that what is most worrying is the denial by authorities that the problem exists and the approach towards addressing the issue shows that ending the problem of manual scavenging is not a priority of the govt.He asserted that the govt must give priority to remove dry latrines wherever they remain. This he said should be a key focus area under the Swachh Bharat Mission.Justice Dhulia expressed shock that manual scavenging and dry latrines still exist in more than 40 districts and said that everyone must feel shame that such a practice continues to exist in our society.Justice Anjana Prakash too expressed concern over the lack of required efforts to end manual scavenging.As the workers shared their lived experiences as manual scavengers, one heard 71 - year - old Mussi Devi from Sitapur district in UP tell how her entire life has passed cleaning dry latrines and even now she is called by families in her area to manually clean-up and dispose of the waste. “When are we going to get freedom from this untouchability?,” asked Mussi Devi and others in her position. Ageing and frail, Devi is also the caregiver for her husband who is paralysed.35 - year - old Muzzafar Ahmed Sheikh from Jammu and Kashmir shared that he is the third generation in his family engaged in manual scavenging in dry latrines. He shared that his community is subjected to untouchability and even their houses are located in a separate cluster. He hails from Wussan village of Ganderbal. A father of a six - year - old, he says, “I want to break free from this identity of being a manual scavenger and I don’t want my son to grow up to do this ever. ”Bezwada Wilson summed up the sentiment of all those seeking justice. “I started the fight when I was 16 and now I am 60. Many things have changed but manual scavenging in dry latrines still remains. We have to end this menace without fail,” he asserted.It is pertinent to point that in the monsoon session of Parliament that concluded in August, in response to a written question in Lok Sabha by Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi, the minister of state for social justice and empowerment Ramdas Athawale said that as per the "Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013 (MS Act, 2013)", a fresh survey has been conducted in all districts of the country during the year 2024-25 in which no manual scavenger has been found. “All the districts of the country have completed the survey and declared themselves as manual scavengers' free,” he said.However, he also added that 58,098 Manual Scavengers (MS) have been identified during two earlier surveys conducted in 2013 and 2018.Clearly differentiating "manual scavenging" and "hazardous cleaning", the minister shared while the later pertains to manual cleaning of a sewer or septic tank, without the employer providing protective gear, cleaning devices and safety precautions, a manual scavenger is defined as someone employed for manually cleaning, carrying, disposing of human excreta in an insanitary latrine.
Article Summary: Safai karmachari andolan (ska) brought together women from uttar pradesh, madhya pradesh, bihar and youth from jammu & kashmir claiming to be engaged in manual cleaning of human excreta in insanitary latrines. The illegal practice still persists in atleast 46 districts of these four states.

Article Title: AIMPLB to launch campaign for protection Constitution and Sharia
Article Text:
The All India Muslim Personal Law Board will launch a movement on Sept 17

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The All India Muslim Personal Law Board will launch a movement on Sept 17 to mobilise public opinion for protection of the Constitution and 'Sharia', religious freedom and rights and dignity of citizens. The Board plans to start the campaign from Jantar Mantar in Delhi and reach out to all faiths over three months.In a statement, the board said that as part of the campaign, a charter of demands will be submitted to the President of India Droupadi Murmu through governors in each state. Besides these issues, the charter will also include demands concerning elimination of hate crimes, prevention of unlawful demolitions, protection of Waqf properties and religious places, and equal enforcement of the law.The Board also proposes to bring out a ‘White Paper’ documenting incidents involving discrimination against Muslims, constitutional and human rights violations and release a comprehensive declaration on the issue of lynching.It said over the past several years conditions have emerged wherein vulnerable and marginalised sections, particularly Muslims, have been subjected to discriminatory treatment.The Board listed concerns ranging from extra-legal bulldozer demolitions, attempts to undermine Muslim Personal Law through Uniform Civil Code to undermining the beliefs of the minority community by making the singing of all six verses of Vande Mataram compulsory, as serious challenges to the Constitution of India, social harmony and national unity.Meanwhile, on the controversy following Kerala’s grand mufti Sheikh Abubakr Ahmad’s comments that women should remain confined to their homes and should not enter the public sphere, arguing that Islam prescribed the purdah system to protect their dignity, AIMPLB spokesperson SQR Ilyas objected to the remarks.Noting that Islam nowhere calls for women to be kept confined to the House for their safety, Ilyas said that the interpretation made by Ahmad is “not correct” and is therefore “misplaced.”He also cited the board’s profile highlighting that there were nearly 30 women in the AIMPLB and asserted that the board was fully in support of the idea of enabling Muslim women to progress which is in keeping with the Islamic teachings.
Article Summary: The all india muslim personal law board will launch a movement on sept 17. Board plans to start the campaign from jantar mantar in delhi and reach out to all faiths. Charter of demands will be submitted to the president of india droupadi murmu through governors in each state.

Article Title: Bus gang-rape case: At minor’s UP village, locked house, silence and a family fleeing intrusion
Article Text:
Local MLA, who visited the village on Monday, said, “People in the village came to know about it probably yesterday." (AI Image)

TOI

TOI

(The victim's identity has not been revealed to protect her privacy as per Supreme court directives on cases related to sexual assault)





AGRA: Fearing intrusion and social stigma, parents of the 17-year-old survivor in the Noida-Delhi bus gang-rape case have locked their house and left their UP village.A villager, who knows the family, toldon Tuesday: “After media persons began visiting our remote village in Mainpuri district seeking details about that horrific incident, they couldn’t take it anymore.” He added: “There’s no one in that house now, the dwelling has fallen silent. ”Another neighbour added: “No one here knew what had happened to the girl. When media persons came here on Monday and told us that she had been raped, everyone was shocked.” He appealed to journalists to avoid repeatedly visiting the place, citing concerns over the survivor’s future and privacy.“Please don’t come again and again to shoot videos or take pictures. She will have to get married in future. By revealing the village and asking people about her, the media has made the matter known here and also the neighbouring areas,” he added.The girl was allegedly sexually assaulted on a moving bus by the vehicle’s driver and conductor on Aug 4. The bus had travelled almost 50 km from Greater Noida to Old Delhi’s Kashmere Gate without being detected. The alleged sexual assault took place while she was travelling from Greater Noida towards Sector 63, police said.After violating her, the bus driver and conductor allegedly dumped her at Ring Road in the Kashmere Gate police station area. The accused duo were later identified as Kuldeep, 39 (bus driver); and Sandeep , 26 (conductor).The area’s SHO told: “The family is safe and have gone to their relatives.”Local MLA, who visited the village on Monday, said, “People in the village came to know about it probably yesterday. When I went there, I found her house locked. Her father’s phone was switched off. I made considerable efforts to speak with the family, but I have been unable to do so thus far.”The MLA added: “I demand the strictest possible punishment for the two accused.” Meanwhile, president of UP State Women Commission, Babita Chauhan, has written to police commissioner of Gautam Budh Nagar for “tough action”.
Article Summary: Parents of the 17-year-old survivor in the noida-delhi bus gang-rape case have locked their house and left their up village. Local mla, who visited the village on monday, said, “people in the village came to know about it probably yesterday."

Article Title: Disha Salian case: Bombay high court orders CBI probe into Sushant Singh Rajput’s ex-manager’s death
Article Text:
The HC said a senior officer of the CBI to conduct the probe.





MUMBAI: Bombay high court on Wednesday pronounced its judgment in the Disha Salian case and directed registration of a first information report (FIR) for her June 8, 2020 death at a suburban Malad building in Mumbai.The Bombay HC appointed a senior officer of the CBI to conduct the probe. The HC also directed not to name anyone as accused in the FIR.“No one shall be treated as an accused unless and until there is suitable material against them, the HC directed.Salian, 28, was a celebrity manager and worked with the late film actor Sushant Singh who died just days later that month on June 14, aged 34 in his Bandra house.On Friday Justices SV Kotwal and RR Bhonsale had reserved for orders her father Satish Salian’s petition to probe her death as a murder arguing through his counsel Nilesh Ojha that “suspicious circumstances’ surrounded it.He had sought investigation by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and said the HC did not lack powers to direct registration of an FIR and probe to ensure complete justice for her family.On Wednesday the HC said : The officer is attached to CBI senior officer in this case and register the FIR, no one be detained unless there's a reasonable suspicion raised, BNSS and Summary report be filed if nothing is found.”At a three day hearing the bench repeatedly questioned the State on why it was still conducting an inquiry under section 174 of the erstwhile criminal procedure code (CrPC)—a provision which it said had limited applicability.The purpose of section 174/175 is limited to ascertaining ‘cause of death’ , as the first line of probe on registration of an Accidental Death Report (ADR).The inquiry that was closed within three months was reopened in 2023 following social media claims, prompting the HC to question the validity of such an extended inquiry.The State represented by chief public prosecutor Shishir Hirey maintained her death was by suicide, following an alleged fall from allegedly the 12th floor of the residential building.Salian’s petition claimed former chief minister Uddhav Thackeray’s son Aditya Thackeray to be an alleged suspect. Salian’s counsel Ojha citing documents, alleged discrepancies and suspicious circumstances to seek a thorough probe as he argued a cognizable offence as claimed by her father, ought to be registered as an FIR as mandated by law.The HC on being shown documents including the Panchanama, photographs of the body, other details from the inquiry so far and raised questions on various aspects it said were “suspicious’’ including whether injuries were consistent with a fall from such height and details regarding clothes.Hirey argued that the injuries included a skull fracture consistent with such fall. Hirey also sought to justify the ADR level inquiry and submitted witness statements and forensics which he said ruled out foul play or any alleged sexual assault on her.The HC clarified that it was not drawing conclusions at this stage but questioned the what had State done for so long jn the last five years, when the prosecution sought dismissal of the father’s plea saying it was belatedly filed .Senior counsel Sudeep Pasbola appearing for Thackeray who had intervened in the matter said the State’s line of probe was not barred by law but also cannot extend indefinitely. Pasbola said Salian has an alternate remedy in law to first go to Magistrate with a private complaint if no FIR is registered and could not directly come to the HC. Pasbola also argued that allegations agaisnt Thackeray were “motivated’’ untenable and stem from a “political rivalry’’.The HC said it was concerned not with any political overtones but only with sanctity of law to provide the family a closure. Ojha argued since the plea was for CBI probe the HC had to be approached as a magistrate lacks the power to direct such probe.Four-and-a half years after it began probing the death of actor Sushant Singh Rajput, last March, the CBI was reported to have closed the case and given a clean chit to actor Rhea Chakraborty, bringing curtains on the case that had gripped the country in 2020.Last year Satish Salian also alleged his daughter was sexually assaulted and murdered and had approached HC seeking the CBI probe into her death as he also alleged both deaths are interconnected and part of a larger conspiracy.
Article Summary: The bombay hc appointed a senior officer of the cbi to conduct the probe. The hc also directed not to name anyone as accused in the fir. Justices sv kotwal and rr bhonsale had reserved for orders her father satish salian’s petition to probe her death as a murder.

Article Title: ​Ram Temple CEO race narrows to three candidates, all from UP
Article Text:
High-level panel submits report for Ram Temple Trust's first CEO

LUCKNOW: The search committee tasked with selecting the next chief executive officer (CEO) of Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust has shortlisted three candidates, who are said to be from Uttar Pradesh The first CEO of the Ram temple is likely to be selected from among the three at a meeting of Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust scheduled at the residence of Trust’s president Nritya Gopal Das in Maniramdas Chhavani on Wednesday.One of the shortlisted candidates is a retired military officer, said a source associated with the process.The three candidates have worked across different parts of the country and have been associated with govt bodies as well as major projects.However, none of them is a bureaucrat or a police officer, contrary to the speculations that Trust could appoint a retired civil servant or a former police officer to the top administrative role.Trust members held discussions on the panel and were satisfied with the credentials and suitability of all three candidates, the sources said.Trust is expected to select one person from the recommended panel and negotiate the remuneration package with the final choice on Wednesday before formally announcing the appointment.The CEO will oversee Trust’s administrative operations, including management of pilgrim facilities, coordination during major religious events and engagement with govt agencies and other stakeholders connected with the functioning of the temple complex and related services.The recommendations follow a comprehensive, technology-enabled recruitment exercise that began with 5,585 applications. The process included multiple rounds of screening, online interactions and in-person meetings with 16 finalists held in Ayodhya on Aug 11 and 12, according to people familiar with the process.The search and selection committee comprised retired Supreme Court judge Justice Pramod Kohli, retired Lt Gen Vishnu Kant Chaturvedi and retired nuclear scientist Suresh Haware, who earlier served as chairperson of Shri Saibaba Sansthan Trust in Shirdi.Kohli said the committee had selected the candidates after a detailed assessment and that Trust would take the final decision.“Among the three people we have selected, the Trust will decide on one person for the CEO’s post. I believe that with Lord Ram’s blessings, the entire process will be completed smoothly,” Kohli said.Search committee secretary Sameer Panda said the shortlisted candidates reflected “the highest calibre of institutional leadership, management expertise, integrity and vision” required for an institution of national and international significance.He said the final report had been submitted and an official announcement would be made in due course.Rejecting speculation about external influence, Panda said no political, religious or social organisation had interfered in the selection process. “No BJP, RSS, VHP or any other organisation ever interfered or recommended anyone’s names for the CEO post,” he said.
Article Summary: High-level panel submits report for ram temple trust's first ceo. Trust is expected to select one person from the recommended panel and negotiate the remuneration package with the final choice on wednesday. The ceo will oversee trust’s administrative operations, including management of pilgrim facilities.

Article Title: Started by a Muslim, a Kolkata Janmashtami turns ‘Hindu-only’
Article Text:
Biplab Bhattacharjee Pandal construction for Janmashtami underway at Kidderpore

KOLKATA: One of Kolkata’s more prominent Janmashtami celebrations in Mominpore — where most of the organisers have been Muslims, making it an example of the city’s multi-cultural spirit — is set to turn into a Hindu-only affair this year.Rakesh Singh, who was BJP ’s (losing) candidate from the Port assembly constituency this year, toldon Tuesday that the celebrations will be organised by “only Hindus” this year as Janmashtami is “a Hindu festival”.Singh, who counted himself as a Congress functionary and used to control Alipore zoo’s labour union as part of the Indian National Trade Union Congress (a Congress affiliate), said he believes in Vishwa Hindu Parishad ’s ideology that “religion belongs to individuals and festivals also belong to those individuals” and was critical of former CM Mamata Banerjee’s oft-repeated statement that “religion belongs to individuals but festivals belong to everyone”.This Janmashtami event, held at the Bhukailash Road-Hussain Shah Road crossing in Kolkata Municipal Corporation’s Ward 79 — part of the Port assembly constituency and bordering CM Suvendu Adhikari’s and former CM Mamata Banerjee’s Bhowanipore constituency — enters its 58th year this time. Prominent patrons have included former city mayor Firhad Hakim and senior Trinamool functionaries Mohammed Alam and Serajul Karim.Singh’s “takeover” of the celebrations comes about a week after VHP addressed the city’s Durga Puja organisers on how to conduct Bengal’s biggest festival. Among the dos and don’ts listed were that there should be no distortion of deities’ images and pandals should be designed to maintain Hindu culture and heritage. VHP also asked puja organisers to strictly prohibit non-vegetarian food inside the core pandal area citing the need to maintain spiritual purity and cleanliness.Singh, who claimed to be both president and chairperson of the Janmashtami organising committee, said, “We cannot demean our traditional culture. People from other religions should definitely visit pandals but it is our duty to protect our religious activities. Janmashtami is a Hindu festival and it should be performed by Hindus only.”According to locals, the Janmashtami event, which is organised by Kidderpore Samaj Kalyan Samity, was initiated by a Muslim social worker, Md Kashim, about six decades ago but faded over the years till another group of Muslim youths revived it after Trinamool came to office in 2011.“Since 2011, we have been organising Janmashtami here. There were around 20 members in the organising committee, and half of them were Muslims. We used to celebrate the event together, distribute prasad and ensure all rituals were followed. But this year, all Muslim faces have been kept out of the committee,” said Md Alam, a Trinamool functionary and former office-bearer of the organising committee.On Monday,found a huge saffron-and-white pandal being erected at the venue. “Muslims used to control Janmashtami here till last year. But this year, it will be exclusively conducted and managed by Hindus. It’s like a cleansing activity,” said an organiser overseeing the pandal construction.
Article Summary: Rakesh singh, who was bjp ’s (losing) candidate from the port assembly constituency this year, toldon tuesday that the celebrations will be organised by ‘only hindus’ singh said he believes in vishwa hindu parishad’s ideology that ‘religion belongs to individuals and festivals also belong to those individuals’ the event, which is organised by kidderpore samaj kalyan samity, was initiated by a muslim social worker, md kashim.

Article Title: Nepal floods bring 'unusual' fish to Bihar, govt warns people not to eat or sell them
Article Text:
A large unusual fish caught in the floodwaters of the Gandak basin being examined by locals at Valmikinagar in West Champaran

BETTIAH: Unidentified and unusual fish swept into the Gandak river and its floodplains by floodwaters from Nepal have prompted the Bihar govt to issue a safety advisory, asking residents of West Champaran and Gopalganj not to consume or trade in such fish until their identity and safety are confirmed.The fisheries division of the dairy, fisheries and animal resources department issued the caution on Tuesday after unusual fish were found in local water bodies and low-lying areas across the flood-hit Gandak basin.Floodwaters from Nepal have entered the Gandak system, inundating several areas of West Champaran and Gopalganj. The department said fish can be swept away from ponds, rivers and other water bodies during floods and carried over considerable distances. During this movement, they may come into contact with contaminated drains, dead animals and other pollutants, raising the risk of contamination by bacteria, viruses and fungi.“Do not consume any unidentified or unusual-looking fish. Until confirmation by the concerned department, an unfamiliar fish should not be considered fit for consumption,” the advisory said.Residents have also been asked not to buy or sell unfamiliar fish caught from floodwaters or assume an unusual-looking species is safe merely because it resembles a commonly eaten fish.Anyone developing vomiting, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, dizziness or breathing difficulty after consuming such fish has been advised to seek immediate medical attention.Wildlife Trust of India director Sameer Kumar Sinha said most fish swept into the Gandak in Bihar following the Nepal floods are believed to be ‘Bagarius bagarius’, commonly known as the goonch catfish and locally called “Gochita”.He said the large freshwater catfish is found in fast-flowing rivers of India, Nepal and parts of Southeast Asia. The carnivorous species feeds on smaller fish, crabs and other aquatic organisms and often hides among rocks in deep stretches with strong currents.Sinha said local communities consume the fish, but it spoils quickly after death and may pose health risks if eaten after deterioration. He urged people to follow the Bihar govt advisory and exercise caution. The species is listed by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) as threatened.
Article Summary: Unidentified and unusual fish swept into gandak river and its floodplains by floodwaters from nepal. Bihar govt issues safety advisory, asking residents of west champaran and gopalganj not to consume or trade in such fish until their identity and safety are confirmed.

Article Title: Srinagar ghost mall turns into Rs 422cr jewel in auction
Article Text:
Srinagar’s stalled commercial complex fetched an eye-popping Rs 421.75 crore (Representative image)

SRINAGAR: For years, grass and weeds had more business at Sangarmaal City Centre than shoppers did. Then came the bidders. A 45-kanal (5.625 acre) parcel around Srinagar’s stalled commercial complex fetched an eye-popping Rs 421.75 crore after an overnight auction far exceeded what govt had pegged.Bidding opened at 11am on Aug 25 for land in front of and behind Sangarmaal, just behind Kashmir Golf Course and opposite Polo View, a pedestrian-only high-street market lined with cafes and boutique stores. One end of the property touches Chunt Khul, a stream running through Srinagar. Dal Lake is about 1km away. Lal Chowk is within easy reach.That mix of location, scale and commercial potential made this largely underused land a prized piece of real estate.By 1.48am on Aug 26, Sangarmaal became one of J&K’s hottest pieces of public real estate, with officials watching the price race far beyond their Rs 200-crore expectations. The highest bid touched Rs 421.75 crore on a full-lease basis.“My heart was racing as the bid was going up and up. It is an important project for J&K and this bid will open investment in the Union Territory after a long time,” an official said Tuesday.Parmesh Construction Company Ltd, a consortium of Pahalgam Green Hotels, a J&K firm and Bhutani Infra Ltd, emerged as the successful bidder.Sangarmaal City Centre traces its roots to 2015, when then CM Mufti Mohammad Sayeed announced it as a new commercial venture meant to give Srinagar a modern skyline.What emerged was an ambitious complex with landscaped areas, fountains, basement and surface parking, lifts and escalators. Its commercial inventory included 62 shops in the main commercial module, 38 spaces in Craft Bazaar, 11 kiosks, two food courts, a restaurant and 11 office spaces.But the dream never got off the ground. Most shops stayed shut. Buyers who acquired units did not open them. Weeds overran the premises, turning what was meant to be a bustling commercial hub into a near-deserted property.Now, a fresh lease could mean a fresh start. The front and rear portions have been offered for development on a full-lease basis, with a multiplex and other commercial facilities proposed.The Sangarmaal auction also set the stage for another high-stakes property bid. At Batamaloo, about 6km away, roughly 70 kanals (8.75 acre) of bus-stand land has remained largely underused and vulnerable to encroachment. Srinagar Development Authority (SDA) is seeking to redevelop it for better use.Bidding opened at Rs 95 crore on Aug 27 and climbed to Rs 305 crore by evening, with Construction Engineers, another J&K consortium, emerging as highest bidder. Batamaloo is also being offered on a full-lease basis, with plans for shopping, office spaces and housing.
Article Summary: A 45-kanal (5.625 acre) parcel around srinagar’s stalled commercial complex fetched an eye-popping rs 421.75 crore. The bid far exceeded what govt had pegged. Sangarmaal city centre traces its roots to 2015, when then cm mufti mohammad sayeed announced it as a new commercial venture.

Article Title: Tribunal alters gay ex-IAF man 'dismissal' to 'routine discharge'
Article Text:
Instead of granting the discharge, IAF initiated a court of inquiry

NEW DELHI: The principal bench of Armed Forces Tribunal (AFT) has converted the order of dismissal of a non-commissioned IAF officer, who confessed to being gay, into a routine discharge.The bench, headed by Justice Rajendra Menon and Justice Rasika Chaube, ruled that substituting dismissal with routine discharge prevents lasting career stigma for the ex-officer seeking employment outside the armed forces.The non-commissioned IAF officer, who had served about 10 and a half years, had applied for a compassionate premature discharge in 2024 to settle down with his partner, disclosing his relationship in an application.Instead of granting the discharge, IAF initiated a court of inquiry. The inquiry concluded he had breached discipline and risked national security by entering into a relationship with a foreigner. The court of inquiry also found him guilty of travelling abroad (Thailand and Sri Lanka) without permission. He was subsequently dismissed from service earlier this year.He then approached AFT principal bench not to challenge IAF's disciplinary right, but to request "dismissal" be changed to a "discharge" so he could seek future civilian employment.The bench held that while dismissal is warranted when rules are breached, exceptions must be considered in this case. "The respondents could have granted discharge to the applicant, but in the garb of maintaining discipline they dismissed him. The effect of both is identical inasmuch as the respondents do not want the service of the applicant."
Article Summary: The bench ruled that substituting dismissal with routine discharge prevents lasting career stigma for the ex-officer seeking employment outside the armed forces. The non-commissioned iaf officer, who had served about 10 and a half years, had applied for a compassionate premature discharge in 2024 to settle down with his partner.

Article Title: CJP’s proposed march on Sep 5 an attempt to create lawlessness before Brics: PIL in SC
Article Text:
“It is for the law enforcing agencies to ensure law and order while acting in accordance with law,” the CJI-led bench said

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday refused to pass any interim orders on two PILs, including one by a retired police officer, seeking deferment of Cockroach Janata Party ‘s proposed march on Sep 5 by alleging that it is intended to create lawlessness ahead of Sep 12-13 BRICS summit in Delhi to deter participation of world leaders.When the petitioners questioned how such a march from the India Gate to the Police Headquarters can take place without permission, A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said there are two issues – one relates to law and order and the other to policy relating to permission to protest marches.“Let the stakeholders talk to them. As of now we have no reason to doubt that everyone would act and behave in a very responsible manner and in a peaceful and lawful manner. Right now, there is no compelling reason for us (the court) to presume that any wrong will happen. It is for the law enforcing agencies to ensure law and order while acting in accordance with law,” the CJI-led bench said.Appearing for one of the petitioners, advocate Syed Rizwan Ahmed said given the BRICS summit, till date no application seeking permission has been given to the authorities. In West Bengal, the previous govt did not give permission to so many protest rallies and the organizers had to move the HC for permission.Why does CJP, an unregistered entity not follow the same process? Are they above law, he asked.“God forbid another mishap, may not be by CJP, but by some mischievous elements take place, it will be covered by international media and deter participation of the foreign country leaders in BRICs,” he apprehended.The bench said, “All these factors are to be considered by some other quarters, not by us. There is nothing we can say right now. If something untoward or alarming happens, then file an application before us, provided the issue falls for determination in judicial domain.”The bench issued notice to the Centre on the two PILs, asked them to supply copies to the SC-constituted High-Powered Committee headed by retired SC judge R Subhash Reddy as well as the office of the solicitor general and posted these for hearing on Sep 10 along with petitions on July 20 incidents during protest march to Parliament, which turned violent resulting in alleged police excesses, injuries to protesters and security personnel and damage to public and private properties.When Ahmed asked whether CJP is above law and its processes, the bench said, “These are issues which are to be taken care of by the law and order enforcing agencies. It is their responsibility to maintain law and order. We expect both sides – protesters and law enforcing agencies - to respect, honour and follow the law of the land.”SC said it has referred a host of issues to the HPC, which is expected to give recommendations one after the other on them. When Ahmed persisted for a hearing on Sep 3 ahead of the proposed march, the bench said the petitioner must approach the Centre and Delhi police on the issue of absence of permission for the march. “Let them consider it,” it said.“There is no organized or identified group before us so that we can request them,” the bench said. Ahmed said that is another problem as CJP has no registered office where notice can be served. Can such an unorganized body hold the capital of the country to ransom, he asked.
Article Summary: The supreme court on monday refused to pass any interim orders on two pils, including one by a retired police officer. The petitioners are seeking deferment of cockroach janata party ‘s proposed march on sep 5 by alleging that it is intended to create lawlessness.

Article Title: BRICS Summit: Delhi Traffic Police issues advisory ahead of motorcade rehearsal
Article Text:
The traffic police has issued a detailed public advisory ahead of BRICS Summit 2026

NEW DELHI: The traffic police has issued a detailed public advisory ahead of BRICS Summit 2026, warning commuters of traffic diversions and restrictions during the motorcade rehearsal on Sept 2. The rehearsal will be held between 10am and 3pm, with traffic regulations planned at 22 diversion points covering more than 35 roads. The summit will be held from Sept 11-13 at Bharat Mandapam.Several key central and south Delhi corridors, including Sardar Patel Marg, Mother Teresa Crescent, Teen Murti Marg, Akbar Road, Tees January Marg, Rajesh Pilot Marg, Subramaniam Bharti Marg, Mathura Road, Moti Lal Nehru Marg, Dr Zakir Hussain Marg, Rani Jhansi Road, Barakhamba Road, Tolstoy Marg, Janpath, among others, will be affected.At major diversion points, commuters will be redirected through alternate routes. They are encouraged to use public transport at this time.

Article Title: OBC creamy layer status: Supreme Court agrees to hear Centre's plea against parents' income-only criteria
Article Text:
SC agrees to hear Centre's plea on OBC creamy layer ruling

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday agreed to hear the Centre's plea challenging the retrospective application of its ruling that parents' income cannot be the sole criterion for determining the creamy layer among Other Backward Classes (OBC) candidates.Also read: Govt seeks 2 years to frame creamy layer criteria for PSU, private staff kids The ruling had held that the status and category of a parent's job must also be considered, along with the Income/Wealth Test, while determining whether a candidate should be excluded from OBC reservation.The matter concerns the criteria used to determine the creamy layer, which identifies relatively advanced sections among OBCs who are excluded from the benefits of reservation.More details awaited.

Article Title: CJP calls off Sept 5 march after SC quashes all FIRs against protesters on Centre's request
Article Text:
What were the three assurances

Why CJP had called for Sept 5 march

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janata Party on Tuesday withdrew its call for a march on September 5 after Supreme Court , on the Centre's request, quashed all FIRs registered across the country against students who participated in the NEET protests."I want to state that in view of the positive assurances of the government of India and the judicial sanctity bestowed upon them today, and in view of the order being passed by this court, the CJP deems it appropriate to withdraw the call for the march on September 5 and looks forward to compliance with today's order," CJP co-convener Sourav Das said during a hearing in the Supreme Court.Chief Justice of India Surya Kant appreciated the CJP's decision, observing that disputes could be resolved if both sides acted in good faith."If both sides show good faith, then all issues can be resolved one by one. There is nothing in the world which is too complicated that it cannot be discussed with an open mind," the CJI said.This comes after Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Centre and Delhi Police, informed the apex court that the Centre remains committed to fulfilling all three assurances given to the leadership of CJP during the meeting between the Centre and the party.The first assurance was that the Centre would not pursue FIRs registered between July 20 and July 25.The second assurance was that no fresh FIRs would be registered in connection with the matter.The third assurance was that the government would pay compensation to students who died by suicide allegedly in connection with the NEET paper leak."Centre is committed to honour the assurance given to the CJP leaders to provide compensation to the families of students who died by suicide after NEET exam cancellation; however, 3 months needed to work out the modalities," Mehta told SC "As of now, we are committed to fulfilling all three assurances," he added.Earlier on Monday, Centre moved the apex court seeking to quash FIR's registered against the student protesters with alleged violence during protests over the NEET paper leak in Delhi and other states.Solicitor general Tushar Mehta mentioned the plea before a bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Monday, seeking the court’s intervention in the matter.The Centre has urged the Supreme Court to exercise its extraordinary powers under Article 142 of the Constitution to quash the FIRs registered against the protesting students.Also read: 'Keeping future of students in mind': Nadda after quashing of FIRs against NEET protesters. CJP had called for a protest march in Delhi on September 5, Teachers' Day. It had accused the Centre of failing to honour the promises made on July 25 to persuade the group to withdraw its 36-day agitation against irregularities in exams and the NEET paper leak.According to the CJP, the march was to be led by families of students who committed suicide following the cancellation of the NEET exam and the subsequent re-test, as well as those who were allegedly subjected to police excesses during the July agitation.
Article Summary: Cockroach janata party on tuesday withdrew its call for a march on september 5. Supreme court quashed all firs registered across the country against students who participated in the neet protests. Centre has urged the supreme court to exercise its extraordinary powers under article 142 of the constitution to quash the firs.

Article Title: SC orders extradition of crypto accused
Article Text:
SC has directed Centre, CBI and Himachal govt to bring Subhash Sharma to justice by getting him extradited

NEW DELHI: Taking note that the main accused in Rs 20,000 crore cryptocurrency fraud case is safely holed up in Dubai for more than a year after duping around 2.5 lakh investors, SC has directed Centre, CBI and Himachal govt to bring Subhash Sharma to justice by getting him extradited. A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran also directed attachment of all movable and immovable property of Sharma and his relatives.An FIR was registered in the case in 2023 and Sharma fled the country but the other accused were arrested in 2025.Granting bail to one of the accused in the case, the bench passed the order to extradite Sharma. It also requested Chief Justice of HP HC to constitute a special court to exclusively deal with this crime.
Article Summary: Sc has directed centre, cbi and himachal govt to bring subhash sharma to justice by getting him extradited. A bench of justices j b pardiwala and k vinod chandran also directed attachment of all movable and immovable property of sharma.

Article Title: Government halves sugar stock limit for dealers to curb hoarding
Article Text:
Govt Tuesday halved sugar stock holding limit for dealers to 2,000 quintals

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Govt Tuesday halved sugar stock holding limit for dealers to 2,000 quintals from Sept 15 till Nov 30, in its bid to ensure adequate availability in the domestic market and prevent hoarding and speculative trading. The move comes as retail prices have moderated to around Rs 63 a kg, but still remain elevated even as ex-mill prices have crashed by more than 20% after govt took a series of steps.At present, stock holding limit for sugar dealers across the country is 4,000 quintals. As per the new order, no sugar dealer can hold any stock for a period exceeding 30 days from the date of receipt of sugar consignments and no dealer can keep over 2,000 quintals of sugar at any time.Govt expects the reduction will facilitate orderly movement of sugar through the supply chain and ensure its continuous availability to consumers at reasonable prices. Meanwhile, govt has undertaken intensive monitoring and physical verification of sugar stocks, covering sugar mills, dealers and traders.
Article Summary: Govt tuesday halved sugar stock holding limit for dealers to 2,000 quintals. Move comes as retail prices have moderated to around rs 63 a kg. Ex-mill prices have crashed by more than 20% after govt took a series of steps.
